findings.title: [P1] Preserve rejection of multiple find roots
findings.body: The new regex captures only the first root and silently consumes additional roots. For example, `find /tmp /home/user -type f -exec rm -rf {} +` sets `_seg_find_root` to `/tmp`, although `rm` also receives files from `/home/user`. Any safety exemption based on the captured root consequently applies to targets outside that root, allowing destructive commands to bypass the intended scope check. The previous root-count check explicitly rejected this case. Require exactly one root or validate every root before granting an exemption.

findings.description: The find-root extraction was changed from 'tokenize the span between find and -exec, require exactly one non-flag root token, else leave _seg_find_root empty (conservative)' to 'take the first whitespace-delimited token after find as the root'. This drops the single-root guard. For a multi-root invocation such as `find /tmp/scratch / -exec rm -rf {} \;`, group 3 captures `/tmp/scratch`, so the `{}` placeholder resolves under a benign root while find actually traverses `/` and rm -rf deletes everything. The old code set _seg_find_root="" when root_count != 1 and fell through to the conservative path. Additionally, the diff comment claims that flag-first forms like `find -L root -exec` 'keep today's conservative behavior', but the new code does not enforce that: `[^;&|)[:space:]]+` happily matches `-L`, `-name`, `!`, or `\(` as the 'root', so `find -L / -exec rm -rf {} \;` yields _seg_find_root="-L" rather than the empty string the old tokenizer produced. Whether `-L` is then treated as a harmless relative path depends on downstream resolution code not in the diff, but the invariant 'unresolvable root => empty' that the rest of the hook was written against is no longer upheld.
findings.failure_mode: An agent (or a prompt-injected agent) issues a destructive find/-exec rm with a benign first root and a dangerous second root, or with a leading flag; the safety hook resolves {} against the wrong path, classifies the rm as scoped/safe, and the destructive command executes unblocked.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the regex change for extracting the span, but restore the single-root invariant: after the match, split BASH_REMATCH[3..] (or re-capture the whole pre-`-exec` span), count tokens up to the first one starting with `-`, `!`, `(`, `)` or `\`, and only assign _seg_find_root when exactly one root token exists AND it does not start with `-`. Alternatively, reject (leave _seg_find_root empty) whenever a second non-flag token appears before the first flag. Add fixtures for `find A B -exec rm -rf {} \;`, `find -L / -exec rm -rf {} \;`, and `find -name x -exec rm -rf {} \;` asserting the conservative/blocking outcome.

findings.description: get_completed_sprints is reverted from counting only sprint-1..N of the current sprint.md to counting every `a2a/sprint-*/COMPLETED` marker on disk. The pre-change file explicitly documents this as bug R-004 (completed=100/total=1). Because determine_state treats `completed_sprints >= total_sprints` as STATE_COMPLETE, stale COMPLETED markers from previous cycles make the workflow report 'All sprints complete' and suggest `/deploy-production` even though the current plan's sprints have not been implemented, reviewed, or security-audited. The reviewing/auditing gates are thus silently skipped in the surfaced workflow. The same value also drives progress_percent, which can exceed 100 and is cached via cache-manager, persisting the wrong state. Minor: `for dir in ${sprint_dirs}` is unquoted, so directory names containing whitespace or glob metacharacters are split/expanded.
findings.failure_mode: After one or more completed cycles, a new sprint plan with fewer sprints than historical COMPLETED dirs is immediately reported as complete; the operator or an automated consumer of `--json` follows the suggested `/deploy-production` without the review/audit sprints having run.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the bounded loop: total=$(get_total_sprints); for ((i=1;i<=total;i++)); do [[ -f "${a2a_dir}/sprint-${i}/COMPLETED" ]] && count=$((count+1)); done. If directory enumeration is desired, filter to sprint IDs present in the current sprint.md and iterate with `while IFS= read -r dir` over `find -print0`/`read -d ''` rather than word-splitting an unquoted variable. Clamp completed to total before computing progress.
